title: IR-Runbook-Credential-Theft
summary: Standard operating procedure for responding to LSASS memory dumps, NTDS.dit extraction, and OS credential dumping indicators.
content:
3. Containment

3.1 Upon confirmation of a credential-theft indicator on a production host, the responding analyst must disconnect the affected endpoint from all network segments immediately, including VPN and wireless interfaces.

Do not power off the machine — this destroys volatile memory needed for forensic capture. Isolation must occur within 5 minutes of confirmed detection.

Proceed to Section 3.2 for memory acquisition steps once isolation is confirmed by the SOC lead.

3.2 Volatile Memory Preservation: Use approved live memory acquisition tooling (e.g., WinPmem or dumpit) before performing process termination or system reboot. Rebooting destroys in-memory artifacts of injected credentials and plaintext passwords in LSASS.

4. Investigation

4.1 Query System Event ID 10 and Sysmon Event ID 10 logs targeting lsass.exe within the past 24 hours. Identify the source calling process, user security identifier (SID), and granted access mask (e.g., 0x1010 or 0x1FFFFF).

4.2 Check running processes, DLL injections, and loaded modules against known credential-theft tooling hashes (Mimikatz, Procdump, Nanodump, Comsvcs.dll mini-dumps).

5. Recovery & Remediation

5.1 Invalidate active Kerberos tickets (KRBTGT reset if domain controller access observed) and force immediate password rotation for all accounts active or cached on the affected host within the exposure window.

steps.title: Isolate host from network
steps.description: Disconnect the affected host from all network segments immediately (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, and active VPN). Do not power off — preserve volatile memory for forensic acquisition.

steps.title: Do not reboot — capture memory image
steps.description: Use approved live memory acquisition tooling before any reboot or process killing. Rebooting destroys volatile evidence of injected credentials and plaintext secrets in LSASS memory.

steps.title: Pull System & Sysmon Event ID 10 for the host
steps.description: Filter for process access events targeting lsass.exe within the last 24 hours to identify the caller process name, granted access mask (e.g. 0x1010), and target PID.

steps.title: Check for known T1003 tooling signatures
steps.description: Cross-reference running processes, spawned scripts, and loaded DLL modules against known credential-dumping tool hashes (Mimikatz, Nanodump, comsvcs.dll).

steps.title: Force credential rotation for all accounts active on host
steps.description: Reset passwords and invalidate Kerberos tickets for any user or service account that logged into the affected host during the compromise window.
